data.title: REG - Saxon Weald Cap plc - Further re related announcement
data.description:
RNS Number : 9478D Saxon Weald Capital PLC 19 November 2026  

Announcement made following an initial, related announcement

This announcement clarifies the announcement released on 19 November 2026 at 10.56am under RNS number 8808D in relation to how customer satisfaction figure is measured, reporting the figure on a 12-month rolling basis rather than a six-month average as in the previous announcement. Commentary explaining the year-on-year reduction in operating margin has also been added. No further changes have been made.

Saxon Weald Group (incl. Saxon Weald Capital Plc) – Trading update for the six months ending 30 September 2026

Saxon Weald Group is today issuing its consolidated trading update for the six months ended 30 September 2026. These figures are unaudited and for information purposes only. Highlights for the period ending 30 September 2026:

  • Saxon Weald owns and manages 7,064 homes;
  • Turnover for the period was £32.7m (September 2025: £29.2m); 
  • Social housing lettings turnover contributed 91% of total turnover (September 2025: 96%); 
  • Operating surplus (including asset sales) for the period was £9.5m (September 2025: £10.6m); 
  • Operating margin on social housing lettings was 26% (September 2025: 29%); 
  • Overall operating margin (including asset sales) was 29% (September 2025: 36%); 
  • Overall operating margin (excluding asset sales) was 28% (September 2025: 30%); 
  • Net margin on shared ownership (first tranche) was 15% (September 2025: -);
  • The surplus after tax for the period was £2.5m (September 2025: £3.9m); 
  • Debt ratio was 53% (September 2025: 51%); and 
  • Return on capital employed for the period was 2.1% (September 2025: 2.4%).

Commenting on the results, Rachel McGoff, Executive Director of Finance & Governance, said:

During the first six months of 2026/27, Saxon Weald has focused on delivering the ambitions set out in our new three-year Corporate Plan, Delivering Better Together, while maintaining our focus on financial resilience and delivering safe, high-quality homes for our customers.

We have continued to strengthen our understanding of the condition of our homes with stock condition survey coverage exceeding 80% by the end of September, on track to meet our target of 90% by the end of 2026/27. This improved data is giving us a stronger evidence base for investment decisions and supporting our longer-term plans for the quality, safety and sustainability of our homes.

We have also continued to invest in energy efficiency. By the end of September, 67% of our homes met our target EPC standard, up from 61%, with grant funding secured to continue our programme of works over the remainder of the year.

Customer satisfaction, measured on a 12-month rolling basis, has remained strong at 84.3% compared with 84.1% at the end of 2025/26. We continue to focus on improving the quality, responsiveness and accessibility of our services.

Our transformation programme has moved into its next phase, bringing together improvements to services, processes, data and technology. During the period, we continued to embed our new customer contact capability and progressed plans to improve our processes, data and systems, with the aim of creating simpler, more responsive services for customers and more efficient ways of working for colleagues.

Alongside investment in existing homes, we have continued to deliver new affordable housing. We completed 55 new homes by the end of September and have a steady future delivery pipeline that balances the need for new affordable homes with investment in our existing homes and our long-term financial resilience.

The lower operating margin compared to September 2025 is a result of more first tranche sales in the first half of the year, which generate a lower operating margin than social housing lettings.

Unaudited Financial Metrics to the 30 September 2026

Statement of comprehensive income

  • Turnover was £32.7m (September 2025: £29.2m); 
  • Turnover from social housing lettings was £29.6m (September 2025: £28.1m); 
  • Operating surplus was £9.5m (September 2025: £10.6m); and 
  • Surplus for the year was £2.5m (September 2025: £3.9m). 

Margins

  • Operating margin[1] on social housing lettings[2] was 26% (September 2025: 29%); 
  • Overall operating margin (incl. asset sales) was 29% (September 2025: 36%); 
  • Overall operating margin (excl. asset sales)[3] was 28% (September 2025: 30%); and 
  • Operating margin on shared ownership (first tranche)[4] was 15% (September 2025: -). 

Key financial ratios

  • EBITDA MRI Interest cover[5] was 128% (September 2025: 134%); and 
  • Gearing[6] was 53% (September 2025: 51%). 

Liquidity

  • 24-month liquidity requirement[7] was £38m (September 2025: £13m); 
  • Cash, short term investments and undrawn facilities[8] were £56m (September 2025: £80m); and 
  • Unencumbered stock (EUV-SH) was £136m (September 2025: £125m). 

Credit rating

  • Moody’s, January 2025, A3 (stable).

This trading update contains certain forward-looking statements about the future outlook for Saxon Weald. These have been prepared and reviewed by Saxon Weald only and are unaudited. Forward looking statements inherently involve a number of uncertainties and assumptions. Although the Directors believe that these statements are based upon reasonable assumptions on the publication date, any such statements should be treated with caution as future outlook may be influenced by factors that could cause actual and audited outcomes and results to be materially different. Additionally, the information in the statement should not be construed as solicitation/recommendation to invest in Saxon Weald's.

data.title: U.S. Leading Indicators Declined in October
data.description:
By Dean Seal

U.S. leading economic indicators fell in October on a drop in building permits, though growth over the past six months is still positive.

The Leading Economic Index, or LEI, published by research group The Conference Board, slid 0.3% to 99.3 after sitting unchanged in September.

The decline was mostly fueled by fewer building permits, which hit their weakest level since May 2020, according to Justyna Zabinska-La Monica, a senior manager at The Conference Board.

"Compared to September and one year ago, permits declined across all categories, including by type of dwelling and region," she said, adding that the Midwest was an exception.

Other negative contributors to the index in October were consumer expectations for business conditions, average hours worked in manufacturing, and manufacturers' new orders for nondefense capital goods, the survey said. Weakness in those components offset gains in others.

However, the LEI's six-month growth rate remained positive, suggesting the economy will continue to expand, but is becoming more dependent on business investment and less on household demand.

The Conference Board now expects real GDP to grow by a 2.3% annualized rate in 2026, with the outlook for 2027 at 2.1%.

The LEI is meant as a predictive index. It is based on 10 components, among them manufacturers' new orders, building permits for new private housing units, stock prices and consumer expectations, and aims to signal shifts in the business cycle.

Write to Dean Seal at dean.seal@wsj.com

data.title: Jupiter Wagons expects sharp margin recovery in FY28
data.description:
Jupiter Wagons, one of India’s leading rolling stock and mobility solutions companies, expects a sharp margin recovery in the next financial year, backed by a large chunk of order book and the wheel line commencing production.

“Going forward, you will start seeing improvements in EBITDA margins. We are quite confident that a large chunk of the order book will come in next year. The impact of this will start becoming visible in FY28,” Jupiter Wagons Managing Director Vivek Lohia told analysts during the company’s Q2 FY27 earnings conference call.

“Additionally, with the wheel line commencing production, we believe FY28 will see the company returning to very strong EBITDA margins. However, over the next few quarters, you will definitely see the EBITDA margins coming back to their FY26 levels,” Lohia said.

The Kolkata-headquartered company reported an EBITDA margin of 12.2 per cent in the second quarter this fiscal compared to 9.7 per cent in the first quarter. It witnessed a healthy sequential improvement in Q2 FY27, with consolidated revenue rising to ₹772 crore from ₹671 crore in Q1 FY27.

“Momentum in the wagon business is returning, and we witnessed a meaningful revival in order booking. During the last few challenging quarters, our established relationships, manufacturing capabilities, and broad portfolio across standard and specialized wagons have enabled us to maintain our competitive position,” he said.

In October this year, Jupiter Wagons secured an order worth ₹1,140 crore from the Ministry of Railways for the manufacture and supply of 2,583 wagons. With these wins, the company’s overall order book increased and now stands at around ₹5,850 crore.

Renewed demand

According to Lohia, these wins reflect renewed demand across customer segments and the strength of the company’s product offering. “Our focus remains on converting the opportunity pipeline into quality orders while maintaining discipline on execution, customer diversification, and returns,” he added.

The company’s subsidiary Jupiter Electric Mobility is expected to turn EBITDA positive in Q3 FY27 and profitable by FY28. Through Jupiter Electric Mobility, the company has expanded its battery energy storage systems business by commissioning a cell-to-battery manufacturing line in Indore, expanding strategic partnerships and deepening customer engagement.

data.title: VIP Industries focuses on premiumisation, product innovation in growth push
data.description:
Luggage company VIP Industries is betting big on premiumisation and distribution expansion as it sharpens its focus on profitable growth. The company posted 15 per cent growth in terms of consolidated revenue from operations in the September quarter.

Atul Jain, Managing Director, VIP Industries told businessline, “We have recorded 15 per cent growth in Q2FY27, which is the second consecutive quarter of growth for us after seven quarters of de-growth. There was also sequential improvement in gross margin despite raw material inflation, supported by a strong focus on premiumisation. We hope to continue to grow in double-digits.”

The company, which narrowed its net loss in Q2, said it remains sharply focused on achieving break-even and has a clear path to profitability.

Jain said the company has been focusing on new innovative launches and premiumisation as key strategies. “We firmly believe that India deserves to travel much better and hence our product strategy is based on consumer insights. We have launched nearly 65 new ranges in terms of products in the first-half and these new products have begun contributing strongly to our business,” he noted. The company’s brand portfolio includes VIP, Skybags, Aristocrat and Caprese.

The company has also ramped up its distribution reach. Jain said in the August-October period, the company expanded distribution reach to nearly 2x the number of outlets earlier. He added that the company is also looking to grow the number of EBOs, which currently stand at about 350 stores.

On online channel growth trends, Jain said, “The online channel has recorded more than 20 per cent growth. The channel is equally important and we are placing our products in it, including premium products.” The online channel currently contributes roughly 25 per cent of the company’s business.

With inflationary pressures growing due to geopolitical tensions, the company has taken three rounds of price hikes in the past six months, totalling to 7-8 per cent.

data.title: BIP Asia Forum and Entrepreneur Day open today
data.description:
HONG KONG, Nov 19, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - The 16th Business of IP Asia Forum (BIP Asia Forum), jointly organised by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC) and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) Government, and the 18th Entrepreneur Day (E-day), organised by the HKTDC, open today at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre. The two annual flagship events feature over 220 speakers and bring together over 440 start-ups, innovation projects and start-up support services. Through forums, seminars, business matching and networking activities, they explore key topics such as intellectual property (IP) financing, artificial intelligence (AI), innovative technology, entrepreneurial development and market expansion, promoting the commercialisation of innovation and cross-sector collaboration, and further strengthening Hong Kong's role as a platform connecting innovation, capital and markets.

Sophia Chong, Executive Director of the HKTDC; Paul Chan, Financial Secretary of the HKSAR Government; Jiang Tong, Deputy Head of the Patent Office of the China National Intellectual Property Administration; Wang Zhicheng, Director General of the Copyright Department of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee; and Dr Changyu Shen, Deputy Director General of the World Intellectual Property Organization, attended the opening session of the BIP Asia Forum this morning and delivered remarks.

Sophia Chong, Executive Director of the HKTDC, said in her welcome remarks: 'Hong Kong published its first Five-Year Plan two months ago in September, laying out a development blueprint for the next five years, aligning with and contributing to China's Five-Year Plan priorities. In this inaugural plan, we reiterated our commitment to boosting our city's standing as a regional IP Trading Centre and International Innovation and Technology Hub. And we at the HKTDC will be proactively supporting these efforts ' not just to help Hong Kong thrive, but to help you all take that next step in growing your business. That is why we are gathering leading voices from across the IP and innovation ecosystems ' policymakers, business leaders, innovators, investors and professionals ' at this event to give you a platform to build and strengthen connections, exchange knowledge and foster impactful partnerships.'

Ms Chong added: 'And just next door, our anchor start-up event Entrepreneur Day extends that journey into entrepreneurship and scale-up, connecting start-ups and innovation projects with investors, business partners and the wider innovation ecosystem. Together with DesignInspire, these concurrent events offer an even broader window into Hong Kong's innovation, entrepreneurship and creative economy.'

Paul Chan, Financial Secretary of the HKSAR Government, said in his opening remarks: 'The National 15th Five-Year Plan supports Hong Kong in deepening its development as a regional IP trading centre. Our own First Five-Year Plan sets out how, including by bringing finance and IP closer together, and by making it less costly, and easier, to hold and trade IP here. Hong Kong's particular role is to connect. Last year, a patent granted in Hong Kong helped to back a securitisation listed in Shenzhen, the first time IP from outside the Mainland has been used in this way. It was small, but it showed that an idea protected on one side of the boundary can raise capital on the other. The traffic can run both ways. We also want Mainland enterprises to use Hong Kong to take their IP to the world.'

Mr Chan added: 'Our shared task is to make them easier to see, to finance and to trade, and to keep our rules fit for an age of AI, so that a good idea born anywhere in Asia can travel the world and prove its worth.'

Leveraging Hong Kong's IP hub advantages to accelerate innovation commercialisation and global collaboration

The theme of the BIP Asia Forum is 'Powering Commercial Success Through IP and Innovation', echoing the national strategy of promoting technological innovation and developing new quality productive forces. It explores how IP and innovation can drive competitive advantages and create long-term value. The Plenary Session I held this morning was titled 'From Sandbox to Scale: Unlocking the Next Phase of IP Financing', discussing the next stage of IP financing development in Hong Kong and consolidating Hong Kong's advantages as a Regional IP Trading and Financing Hub connecting the Chinese Mainland and global markets. Anita Ou, Managing Director, Head of Enterprise Banking, Commercial Banking, the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited said: 'Intellectual property financing can serve as an enabler of Hong Kong's long-term market development. It can support the growth of local innovative industries and Chinese Mainland enterprises with global ambitions to monetise their IP via Hong Kong, as well as help traditional businesses invest in technology, product design and automated production processes as they transform for the future. The successful outcomes of the IP Financing Sandbox have also given the banking industry valuable experience in unlocking financing based on IP with appropriate risk management. To build on this progress, we look forward to closer collaboration across the IP financing ecosystem to encourage wider adoption and further strengthen Hong Kong's growing role as an IP financing and trading hub'

Hong Kong is actively developing into an International Innovation and Technology Hub and a Regional IP Trading Centre. This year, the Forum introduces the Tech Chapter series, focusing on technology transfer, IP investment, commercialisation of innovation achievements, and entrepreneurial development. The Tech Chapter kicked off with the Plenary Session II, titled 'Reinventing Sports: Unlocking IP Value Inside and Beyond the Stadium', echoing the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) World Intellectual Property Day 2026 theme 'IP and Sports: Ready, Set, Innovate'. Drawing on perspectives from technology innovation, commercial operations and athlete brand management, speakers examined how IP powers the transformation of the sports industry. They discussed how intangible assets can be leveraged as strategic commercial capital to unlock sustainable value and growth beyond competition. Filipe Trigo Gon'alves, Chairman of Asia Partner, who introduces the FIFA Museum to Hong Kong, said: 'We use Hong Kong as our platform, and then to reach the rest of the world. We opened the FIFA store in Hong Kong, and then we moved into other markets. This is the easiest way, because Hong Kong is very dynamic, very international and very secure as a place to build these kinds of concepts and be successful in the different regions in Asia.'

Other sessions of the Tech Chapter will also explore how IP can foster innovation cooperation, industrial upgrading, and market expansion, echoing Hong Kong's broader agenda of promoting innovation and technology development and intellectual property trading.

To help enterprises seize global development opportunities, the session 'IP Protection & Global Commerce in the Greater Bay Area: Emerging Industry Breakthroughs and Commercial Success Driven by Institutional Innovation', co-organised by the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation (Guangdong Intellectual Property Administration) and the Forum, was held today to examine IP system innovation in the Greater Bay Area, transformation of technological achievements, financial empowerment, and how deeper integration of IP, innovative technology, and capital markets can accelerate the cultivation of new industries, new business forms, new business models, and high-quality enterprise development. The 'IP Go-Global Business Matching Session' also returned this year, providing one-on-one business matching for Chinese Mainland enterprises pursuing international expansion. The session connected participants with Hong Kong IP professionals and experts to strengthen global IP deployment, enhance risk management capabilities and support cross-border business growth.

Tomorrow, the Tech Chapter will feature several key sessions. Among them, the breakout session 'Play Beyond Boundaries: IP Strategies in the World of Play' will invite Johnny Sze, CEO of Eastcolight (Hong Kong) Limited; Jessica Qian, Senior Director, Licensing Consumer Products, APAC & MENA, Hasbro; and Ivan Wong, Head of Consumer Products & Experiences, Asia, Moonbug Entertainment to share how enterprises can harness IP to foster innovation, deepen audience engagement and create new growth opportunities across markets and generations. Meanwhile, 'IPHatch Asia - Reimagining IP Commercialisation: The Power of Entrepreneurship' will invite guests including Monica Hong, Investor at Betatron Venture Group to explore how start-ups and IP owners can accelerate technology transfer and bring innovations to market through strategic partnerships, unlocking new commercial opportunities and business value.

Another breakout session is the WIPO-led panel discussion 'Empowering Business Success: Practical Solutions for AI and IP Licensing'. This session will explore emerging opportunities and challenges brought by AI, copyright licensing, and digital business development. Opening remarks will be delivered by Dr Changyu Shen, Deputy Director General of WIPO, and David Wong, Director of Intellectual Property of the HKSAR Government. Featured speakers include Ignacio de Castro, Director of the WIPO Arbitration and Mediation Center, and Yuhong Zhou, Legal Director of Tencent Music Entertainment Group, who will share insights on how IP licensing and dispute resolution mechanisms can facilitate the responsible deployment of AI technologies and accelerate their commercial application.

In their pursuit of market expansion and sustainable growth, local brands are increasingly transforming IP into a source of competitive differentiation. The breakout session 'Hong Kong Brands Reimagined: The Power of Strategic IP' will focus on how Hong Kong brands can leverage IP to drive innovation, expand markets, and enhance long-term commercial value. The Forum has invited Adrian Cheung, Executive Director, General Counsel, Market Innovation and Development Director of the Garden Company Limited; Renee So, Director of Kung Wo Bean Curd Factory; and Kevin Kwong, Chief Business Officer of 9GAG and MemeStrategy Inc, to share their experiences and examine how enterprises can leverage IP strategies to strengthen market positioning and capture new development opportunities. Their signature products and merchandise will also be showcased in the Forum's exhibition area, illustrating how IP can foster brand upgrading and business development.

In addition to a series of forum sessions exploring IP financing, innovation and technology development, and business growth strategies, this year's Forum will facilitate connections between innovative solutions, investors, professional service providers and potential business partners through exhibitions and networking initiatives. The Innovation and IP Market will display innovative technologies and research achievements from the Chinese University of Hong Kong, the Hong Kong Baptist University, the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, the Education University of Hong Kong, and other Hong Kong research institutions, while bringing together IP, legal, and professional service organisations to promote the commercialisation and application of innovation achievements. New this year, the GoGlobal Connect Zone addresses the growing international needs of Chinese Mainland enterprises by providing one-stop access to legal, financial and corporate service providers, empowering businesses to expand globally through Hong Kong.

E-day focuses on AI and global expansion to help start-ups explore worldwide business opportunities

Organised by the HKTDC, Entrepreneur Day is a flagship start-up event under the theme 'Where Start-up Dreams Take Flight', bringing together over 370 start-ups, innovation projects, and start-up support services from 13 countries and regions. The event covers four major areas: AI, deep technology, green and sustainable technology, and health technology. During the event, multiple seminars, start-up pitching sessions, and networking activities will be held, inviting business leaders and industry experts from around the world to share the latest technology trends and market insights, helping start-ups explore global business opportunities.

The three thematic zones of E-Day include the Start-up and Innovation, University Spin-off, and Boosters. Among them, the Hong Kong Innovation Pavilion organised by the Digital Policy Office of the HKSAR Government showcases over 35 cutting-edge solutions from this year's Hong Kong ICT Awards, covering smart mobility, digital entertainment, and smart living technologies. The pavilion hosted by the Home and Youth Affairs Bureau brings together over 50 start-ups supported by the Funding Scheme for Youth Entrepreneurship in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. The projects covered green technology, education technology, and biotechnology, addressing social needs such as sustainable development, talent cultivation, and healthcare through innovative technology solutions and demonstrating the innovative capabilities and development potential of young entrepreneurs in the Greater Bay Area. Members of the Alliance of Hong Kong Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurial Bases in the Greater Bay Area will also display entrepreneurship support services, allowing more people to understand the development prospects, policy support, and resource networks for entrepreneurship in the Greater Bay Area. In addition, the Asia Exhibition of Innovations and Inventions Hong Kong (AEII), co-organised by the Hong Kong Exporters' Association and Palexpo, the organiser of the International Exhibition of Inventions Geneva, has gathered over 170 Asian innovation and invention projects this year, demonstrating the vitality and development potential of the region's innovation and technology sector.

In line with the growing trend of sports tech in recent years and echoing the sports IP theme of the BIP Asia Forum, E-Day has specially designated sports tech as one of its key topics this year, organising the T-Chat session 'Turning Sweat into Startups: The Next Wave of SportsTech Innovation'. The session invited former athletes-turned-entrepreneurs and industry representatives to explore how technologies such as AI and data analytics can drive innovation in the sports industry and open up new business models and market opportunities. Alvina Chen, Founder and CEO of Feldspar, said: 'What we are doing with AI coaching and intelligence is about supplementing what coaches already do. A professional team might traditionally need 10 coaches, data scientists and biomechanics experts. With AI, perhaps that team can now become two or three people. We can also establish accurate baselines for athletes, giving us much better insight into injury prevention. What we are doing is bridging the gap between laboratory testing and live training.'

AI applications are another key topic at this year's E-Day. Riding the wave of AI development, the seminar 'The Rise of the One-Person Unicorn: How AI Is Creating the Next Generation of Global Entrepreneurs' explored how generative AI and AI agents are transforming entrepreneurial models. Judy Zhang, Executive Director of Pegasus Tech Ventures, said: "With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence technology, the 'one-person company' entrepreneurial model has expanded from its previous focus on internet-based businesses to specialised fields such as financial technology, biotechnology, and physical AI. The advantage of small teams lies in their ability to focus on specific industries, transforming practical experience into market-oriented solutions rather than merely providing general information.' The 'Build Your AI-Powered Team' Workshop focused on human-machine collaboration and enterprise application scenarios, exploring how to leverage AI to enhance operational efficiency and competitiveness.

In addition to innovative technology topics, E-Day also emphasises cultivating an entrepreneurial mindset and spirit of enterprise. The special forum 'Building Beyond Your First Business: Lessons from Hong Kong's Serial Entrepreneurs', co-organised with OCBC Hong Kong, invites several local serial entrepreneurs to share their entrepreneurial journeys, to explore how entrepreneurs can seize opportunities, respond to challenges in a rapidly changing market environment, and build on their experience to launch new ventures.

E-Day also promotes regional cooperation and market expansion through various activities. The GBA Tripartite Roundtable: 'Empowering GBA Startups to Expand into ASEAN with Hong Kong as a Super-connector and Super Value-adder' explored development opportunities in the ASEAN market and how Hong Kong can assist Greater Bay Area start-ups in expanding into overseas markets. In addition, the '2026 Jiangsu-Hong Kong Technology and Innovation Cooperation Matchmaking Conference' promoted exchanges and cooperation between Hong Kong universities, research institutions, and Jiangsu enterprises, driving technology cooperation and the commercialisation of innovation achievements.

Start-up Express International connects the global start-up ecosystem

This year, the ten winning start-ups participating in Start-up Express International come from the Chinese Mainland, Germany, Indonesia, Korea, and other regions, focusing on areas such as AI, green technology, and health technology. Several of the winning start-ups are participating in E-Day, where they will showcase their innovative solutions and entrepreneurial achievements through exhibitions and sharing sessions. They will also connect with Start-up Express participants and professional judges to exchange entrepreneurial experiences and explore development opportunities in Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area. Since its launch in 2022, Start-up Express International has been helping non-Hong Kong start-ups establish business connections and expand into the Greater Bay Area and international markets, promoting exchanges between local and global start-ups. It complements Hong Kong's active efforts to leverage its advantages as an international innovation and technology hub and strengthen connections across the global entrepreneurial ecosystem.

In addition, DesignInspire will be held from 18 to 21 November at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, concurrently with the BIP Asia Forum and E-Day, bringing together local and international design elites to present wonderful design experiences for the industry and the public. The three events held concurrently cover creative design, intellectual property, and entrepreneurial development, promoting cross-sector exchanges and cooperation, and showcasing Hong Kong's complete innovation ecosystem from creativity and innovation to market application.

data.title: Philly Fed Index Plunges To Six-Month Low In November
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia released a report on Thursday showing regional manufacturing was less widespread in the month of November but continued to expand overall.

The Philly Fed said its diffusion index for current general activity plunged to 6.3 in November after tumbling to 20.9 in October.

While a positive reading still indicates growth, economists had expected the index to show a much more modest decrease to 17.0.

With the much bigger-than-expected decrease, the Philly Fed Index continued to give back ground after reaching a five-year high of 47.4 in August, tumbling to its lowest level since hitting a negative 0.4 in May.

The extended pullback by the headline index came as the new orders index fell to a negative 0.4 in November from a positive 4.3 in October, hitting its lowest level since May.

Meanwhile, the shipments index jumped to 25.7 in November from 15.3 in October, offsetting most of the previous month's decline.

The number of employees index also rose to 11.6 in November from 9.1 in October, continuing to suggest overall gains in employment.

On the inflation front, the report said the prices paid index jumped to 58.2 in November from 43.2 in October, while the prices received index climbed to 47.0 in November from 40.1 in October.

The Philly Fed also said the diffusion index for future general activity crept up to 33.6 in November from 33.0 in October.

A separate report released by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on Monday showed a substantial pullback by its reading on regional manufacturing activity in the month of November.

The New York Fed said its general business conditions index plunged to 7.8 in November after surging to 25.5 in October. Economists had expected the index to show a much more modest decrease to 18.0.

Meanwhile, the report said firms grew more optimistic conditions would improve in the months ahead, with the index for future business conditions jumping to 28.9 in November from 21.0 in October.
